goal: Provide a deterministic offline harness that can describe, edit, regenerate, validate, visually review, and export procedural mesh kits through replayable JSON transactions.
target: A reusable Three.js mesh-edit factory with a declarative mesh-program AST, live JSON injection, incremental evaluation, ten-angle review orchestration, and topology-gated export.
selectionReason: The decisive complexity is coordination across independently meaningful AST, evaluator, live-state, renderer, validator, reviewer, and exporter components. Mathematical generation and guided review are explicit subcomponents.

rejectedTypes.reason: Deterministic geometry rules alone do not provide transactional editing, incremental state, review evidence, or export coordination.
Visual judgment is required, but review alone does not define the reusable editing and generation system.
No authoritative measured dataset is currently required to calibrate the first kit; reference images guide appearance but do not define geometry truth.
The requested edits, topology constraints, and variations can be expressed explicitly without model training.

sources.provenance: Captured as kit/mesh-program.json with its accepted transaction history
sources.license: User-owned sandbox work; external reuse terms unresolved

User-supplied and approved visual direction in the current conversation

inputs: RFC 6902 JSON Patch transaction with base revision
named seed and deterministic random streams

parameters.name: meshProgram.nodes[*].params
parameters.range: Declared per node by schema and kit constraints

seedPolicy.algorithm: Declared uint32 PRNG with FNV-1a-derived named streams and path-stable sampling

stages.validation: Schema, stable IDs, references, types, ranges, and acyclic dependency graph pass

stages.output: incrementally cached Three.js geometry, materials, and scene state
stages.validation: Only dirty nodes and their dependents recompute; repeat hashes match
Patch is authorized by schema, evaluated in isolation, and rolled back on failure
Topology, winding, finite values, UVs, bounds, budgets, and determinism gates pass

stages.input: eligible candidate and fixed capture profile
stages.output: ten-angle orbit, hero render, and contact sheet
stages.validation: Every view is present, nonblank, consistently framed, and hash-recorded

stages.input: incumbent, challengers, hard-gate reports, and comparable captures
stages.output: accept, reject, or retain-incumbent decision with reasons
stages.validation: No technically failed candidate can win; human or agent visual judgment is recorded separately from synthetic scores

stages.output: GLB, mesh-program JSON, manifest, and evidence package
stages.validation: Export reimports, matches expected structure, and retains source revision and hashes

authorities: Recorded human or agent visual comparison against the approved reference
claims: Every committed edit is replayable from the base document and transaction log
A failed patch cannot mutate committed live state
Dirty-node evaluation is equivalent to a clean full rebuild
Winning structural meshes satisfy the declared topology and winding gates
Final exported artifacts correspond to the accepted AST revision

humanReview.authority: User approval is final; the assistant may choose an interim incumbent when evidence is retained

delivery.format: Repository-local offline ESM package, browser preview, CLI, kit folder, JSON schemas, tests, and reproducible evidence outputs

constraints: Offline asset-production tool; it is not added to the public browser Kit registry
Plain Node ESM and existing rendering dependencies; no mandatory framework
Stable IDs and schema versions for all AST nodes and transactions
Preview edits never overwrite committed state
Hard technical gates run before visual review
Rejected candidates and failed attempts remain in evidence
Core harness contains no Triceratops-specific anatomy rules
The reviewed revision 45 candidate remains the incumbent until a challenger is explicitly accepted
unknowns: Final animation and rigging contract is outside the first harness scope
Whether Blender-native export/edit round-tripping is required after GLB proof
Whether later kits need texture baking beyond procedural vertex colors and generated maps
Whether a remote vision reviewer will be available; the initial review adapter must support assistant or human decisions
